propositions: BindingStore's 799-line module conflates byte persistence, lifecycle policy, recovery, rotation, and comment identity with no cohesive owner for new safety rules, causing production code to mutate inner entries via shallow all_bindings() query

Interrupted retirement completion requires a journal-free durable tombstone rule where live forward/reverse pairs are removed only when tombstone and both identities agree, and only explicit unretire revokes that intent

Three internal owners (repository/unit-of-work, lifecycle policy, recovery) must be extracted behind one unchanged public BindingStore facade with all stored formats, imports, signatures, and exact JSON serialization preserved
Live recovery must run after staleness validation but before remote issue fetch and lifecycle mutation to prevent interleaving new liveness evidence with completion operations
Automatic liveness signals (absent 404 count, same-key confirm, clear-absent) cannot override durable tombstone intent; only explicit unretire removes it and eliminates the completion candidate

Slices 1-3 extract three owners across nine tasks with held-out RED-first TDD evidence, mutation-discovered oracle gaps, and four documented-but-unimplemented behaviors corrected rather than implemented
